facts.c: The tourist (T) e-visa is single entry and costs USD 30.
facts.q: Visa T Enter Type Single entry only Fee USD 30

facts.c: The T e-visa is valid for 3 months from issue and allows a stay of 1 month, processed in 3 business days.
facts.q: 3 months(starting from the date of issue) Length of Stay 1 month Processing time 3 business days

facts.c: The T e-visa needs a passport valid for more than six months on entry, a digital passport photo (JPEG or PNG) and a Visa or MasterCard credit card.
facts.q: Passport validity of more than six months balance at the time of entry, a recent passport-size photo in digital format (JPEG or PNG format), a valid credit card (Visa/MasterCard).

facts.c: Only nine ASEAN countries (Laos, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Brunei, Myanmar) are listed as visa-exempt; Bangladesh is not.
facts.q: Visa Exemption Laos, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Brunei Darussalam, Myanmar

facts.c: In April 2025 the e-visa office announced the E-class (ordinary/business) e-visa is available to applicants from all countries.
facts.q: "Visa Type E” for our customers from all countries to apply for a Cambodia visa online

facts.c: The e-visa application steps are: Application menu, security code, personal, passport and travel details, review, payment.
facts.q: Click on “Application” menu. Security Verify, Enter the correct code which display in the box. Application, Fill in personal info, passport detail and travel detail. Review, Please review all your information before proceed to Payment. Payment, Choose your payment method that you prefer.

facts.c: A wrong photo can be changed after submission by emailing it to info@evisa.gov.kh with the reference number.
facts.q: Please send the photo to info@evisa.gov.kh together with your reference number.

facts.c: The e-visa office in Phnom Penh can be reached on (855) 23 224 973 and (855) 99 334 973 (Khmer, English).
The tourist visa (T) is for leisure travel and employment on it is prohibited.
facts.q: General travelers to Cambodia for leisure activities; employment is prohibited.

facts.c: The tourist visa is single entry, valid three months from issue, and extendable once.
facts.q: Tourist Visa (T) Entry Type Single Validity Three (3) months from the date of issue Length of Stay One (calendar) from the date of entry Extension Status Yes, extendable (once)

facts.c: Tourist visa supporting documents: a flight, bus or boat ticket and an accommodation booking.
facts.q: Flight/bus/boat ticket, accommodation booking

facts.c: The business visa (E) is for people who accepted a job offer or invitation from a registered Cambodian company or organisation, and also for trainees, interns and students.
facts.q: Those who have accepted an employment offer in Cambodia, received an invitation from a registered company or organization in Cambodia, or are being sent to Cambodia for business purposes by a registered company or organization, also for trainees, interns and students.

facts.c: The E visa needs a letter of invitation or job offer/contract from a company or organisation in Cambodia.
facts.q: Letter of invitation or job offer/contract from a company or organization in Cambodia

facts.c: The E visa allows one month's stay from entry and is extendable with multiple options.
facts.q: One month from the date of entry Extension Status Yes, extendable (multiple options)

facts.c: Diplomatic (A) and Official (B) visas are only for diplomatic, official/service passport holders and UN laissez-passer holders on official missions.
facts.q: This visa is issued to non-immigrant foreigners holding Official/Service Passports who are undertaking official government missions

facts.c: The Courtesy visa (C) is for members of international NGOs registered with an MoU with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
facts.q: Members of registered international NGOs.

facts.c: The Khmer visa (K) is for people of Khmer origin or Cambodian ancestry, including children of Cambodian citizens holding a foreign passport.
facts.q: Those who are of Khmer origin or have Cambodian ancestry, including children born to Cambodian citizens (by birth or naturalization) who now hold a foreign passport.

facts.c: Foreigners married to Cambodian citizens are not eligible for a K visa and must apply for a T or E visa.
facts.q: Foreign nationals married to Cambodian citizens are not eligible for a K Visa and should apply for a T or E-class visa instead

facts.c: Visas are valid for entry within three months of issue; length of stay starts at immigration and is counted by calendar month.
facts.q: Your permitted length of stay begins the moment you pass through immigration at any entry point in Cambodia and is counted by the (calendar) month

facts.c: From 3 October 2026 Cambodia stopped issuing visa stickers; all visas are issued digitally.
facts.q: effective 3 October 2026 . All visa applications submitted (online or through the Embassy) after this date will be processed and issued digitally. Visa stickers will no longer be placed in passport books.

facts.c: There are three ways to get a visa: through an embassy by email, online on the e-visa portal, or on arrival.
facts.q: There are three options to obtain a visa:

facts.c: Express processing is not available; processing usually takes 3 business days and applications made more than a month ahead wait until the one-month window opens.
facts.q: Express or rush processing is unavailable. Although processing is usually within 3 business days

facts.c: The e-visa is sent by email and can be tracked, updated or downloaded under 'Check and Change' using the reference number.
facts.q: You can also track your application status, update pending details, or download your e-Visa directly on the portal under the " Check and Change " section.

facts.c: Visa on arrival remains available at all international airports and border checkpoints.
facts.q: Visa on Arrival (VoA) remains available at all international airports and international border checkpoints.

facts.c: Land border crossings between Cambodia and Thailand remain closed until further notice.
facts.q: land border crossings between Cambodia and Thailand remain closed until further notice.

facts.c: An e-visa bought directly online is not accepted at some small border checkpoints, while an embassy-issued electronic visa works at any international checkpoint.
facts.q: Visas obtained directly online have restricted entry coverage

facts.c: The e-visa is run only by the E-Visa Office of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, not by embassies; questions go to that office.
facts.q: The e-Visa service is exclusively operated by the E-Visa Office within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Cambodia and is not handled by Cambodian embassies abroad

facts.c: Visa on arrival is offered at all international entry points but not every nationality is eligible.
facts.q: The last option is Visa on Arrival at all international entry points (not every country is eligible).

facts.c: The e-Arrival is not a visa; travellers with a visa must still submit it.
facts.q: Yes. Cambodia e-Arrival is not a visa; it collects information about immigration, health and customs.

facts.c: EB (business) extensions are for employees, freelancers, volunteers and dependents of EB holders, for 1, 3, 6 or 12 months.
facts.q: Employees, freelancers, volunteers; dependents of EB holders 1, 3, 6, 12 months

facts.c: A dependent on an EB extension adds proof of relationship and the EB holder's letter.
facts.q: Dependents: add proof of relationship + holder’s letter.

facts.c: An EB extension does not give the right to work; a work permit is still required.
facts.q: Does not grant the right to work — a work permit is still required.

facts.c: EG (job-seeker) extensions are for people looking for work, for 1, 3 or 6 months, generally single entry.
facts.q: Those looking for work 1, 3, 6 months Generally single-entry

facts.c: ES (student) extensions are for students at a registered Cambodian school, need an enrolment letter and proof of funds, for 1, 3, 6 or 12 months.
facts.q: Students at a registered Cambodian school 1, 3, 6, 12 months

facts.c: The ES extension needs an enrolment letter from a registered school and proof of funds.
facts.q: Enrollment letter from a registered school + proof of funds required.

facts.c: 1- and 3-month E-class extensions are single entry; 6- and 12-month ones are multiple entry.
facts.q: 1 & 3 mo: single-entry 6 & 12 mo: multiple-entry

facts.c: The retirement extension (ER) needs age 55 or over, proof of retirement and sufficient funds.
facts.q: To be eligible, you must be 55 years of age or older

facts.c: E-class extensions are applied for inside Cambodia at the immigration office or through a visa agent.
facts.q: Once in Cambodia, apply at the immigration office or through a visa agent.

facts.c: Foreigners married to Cambodians do not automatically get Khmer nationality and cannot get the K visa; they need a T or E visa.

facts.c: Bavet (Svay Rieng) on the Vietnam border is open and accepts e-visas.
facts.q: Bavet (Svay Rieng) Vietnam Yes Yes

facts.c: All land border crossings between Cambodia and Thailand (including Poipet, Cham Yeam and O Smach) are physically closed until further notice.
facts.q: All land border crossings between Cambodia and Thailand remain closed until further notice.

facts.c: Bangladesh is covered by the Royal Embassy of Cambodia in New Delhi (with India, Iran, Nepal and Sri Lanka).
facts.q: New Delhi, India Bangladesh, India, Iran, Nepal, Sri Lanka

facts.c: Standard tourist and business visas can typically be requested from any Cambodian embassy regardless of where the applicant lives.
facts.q: Standard Tourist and Business Visas can typically be requested from any Royal Embassy of Cambodia, regardless of your current location.

facts.c: Every traveller must fill in the e-Arrival, even with a visa; it is not a visa.
facts.q: All travelers are required to fill in the Cambodia e-Arrival even if they have been granted VISA.

facts.q: No, it is completely free for all travelers to fill in the e-Arrival Card by the official website or mobile application.

facts.q: You may register and submit application within 7 days prior to your arrival into the Kingdom of Cambodia.

facts.q: Take a screenshot or download your QR code before closing or exiting the e-Arrival Card website.

facts.c: https://arrival.gov.kh is the only official e-Arrival website.
facts.q: The https://arrival.gov.kh is the only official website of the Cambodia e-Arrival Card.

facts.q: rejecting “Cambodia-e-arrival.online” as a legitimate website recognised by the Royal Government or operated by the GDI

facts.c: No service fee is charged for the e-Arrival, except the visa fee.
facts.q: there is no service fee required, except for the visa fee

facts.c: The Royal Embassy of Cambodia in New Delhi (A-1/309, Safdarjung Enclave, New Delhi 110029; +91 11 41717136 / 41717143; camemb.ind@mfaic.gov.kh) is accredited to Bangladesh.
facts.q: Royal Embassy of Cambodia A-1/309, Safdarjung Enclave, New Delhi 110029 Tel : +91 11 41717136 / 11 41717143 Email : camemb.ind@mfaic.gov.kh

facts.c: From 1 January 2025 the T e-visa fell from USD 36 to USD 30 and the E e-visa from USD 42 to USD 35, so older guides quoting USD 36 are out of date.
facts.q: Tourist (T) e-Visa: Reduced from 36 USD to 30 USD

facts.c: The E e-visa fell from USD 42 to USD 35 on 1 January 2025.
facts.q: Ordinary (E) e-Visa: Reduced from 42 USD to 35 USD

facts.c: A tourist visa on arrival is now processed electronically, with a digital visitor pass sent by email instead of a sticker or stamp.
facts.q: immigration processes the entry electronically and a digital visitor pass or confirmation is sent by email

facts.c: Claims that a tourist visa can easily be turned into an E-class visa after arrival are not the standard or official pathway.
facts.q: travelers should be wary of anyone claiming that a tourist visa can easily be transformed into an ordinary E-class visa after arrival. That is not the standard or official pathway

facts.c: Foreigners must be registered in FPCS (Foreigners Presence in Cambodia System) at their address; hotels usually do it, private rentals and guesthouses less reliably.
facts.q: Hotels usually handle this registration automatically

facts.c: Foreigners not registered in FPCS may be unable to extend their visas.
facts.q: foreigners not registered in the database may be unable to extend their visas

facts.c: In July 2025 the GDI said Cambodia has no policy of denying visas, entry or extensions to any nationality, but officers apply stricter checks.
facts.q: Cambodia does not have a policy of denying visas, entry, or visa extensions to any nationality

facts.c: Officers may refuse entry or extensions to anyone without a clear travel history and purpose, the means to support themselves and a guarantor.
facts.q: having a clear travel history and purpose, demonstrating the ability to financially support oneself during the stay, providing a guarantor to resolve potential issues

facts.c: Cambodia deported nearly 5,000 foreigners of 88 nationalities in the first half of 2025.
facts.q: Cambodia deported nearly 5,000 foreigners during the first half of 2025, spanning over 2,000 cases involving 88 nationalities

facts.c: The tourist visa gives 30 days on entry plus one 30-day extension, about 60 days in total, after which the holder must leave.
facts.q: You can stay 30 days on entry, then get one 30-day extension for about 60 days total. After that, T-class holders must leave the country.

facts.c: Tourist visa extensions cannot be done online; they are done at the immigration office in Phnom Penh or through a licensed visa agent.
facts.q: No, tourist visa extensions cannot be processed online. The options are the immigration office in Phnom Penh or a licensed visa agent.

facts.c: Ordinary-passport visa exemption covers only the other ASEAN states, the Maldives and Seychelles; everyone else needs a T visa by e-visa or on arrival.
facts.q: Ordinary passports of the 9 other ASEAN states (14 or 30 days), the Maldives (30 days) and Seychelles (15 days) are exempt

facts.c: From 1 September 2026 visa-on-arrival fees can be prepaid online with the e-Arrival for Techo, Siem Reap Angkor and Sihanoukville airports.
facts.q: Cambodia began allowing online prepayment of visa-on-arrival fees on Sept. 1

facts.c: In 2026 the GDI ran nationwide spot checks of visas, work permits and address registration; landlords face fines of up to USD 1,000 per undocumented foreign occupant.
facts.q: Property owners can be fined up to $1,000 per undocumented occupant.

facts.c: Foreigners must report a change of address to local police within 24 hours.
facts.q: Other foreigners must report address changes to local police within 24 hours.

facts.c: Expats reported in 2022 that converting tourist visas into E-class extensions (EB, ER, ES, EG) was suspended, so people must enter on an ordinary (E) visa and extend within 30 days.
facts.q: As per today the converting of tourist visas into E-extensions (EB, ER, ES and EG) has been suspended.

facts.c: After the single tourist extension, a person must leave and re-enter on a new tourist or ordinary visa.
facts.q: After you have extended your tourist visa once for 30 days you leave the country and come back on either another tourist visa (60 days total) or an Ordinary visa if you want to stay longer.

facts.c: Foreign students at Cambodian institutions need an E-class visa extended as a student (ES) visa, in steps of 1, 3, 6 or 12 months.
facts.q: Foreign students enrolled in Cambodian educational institutions must obtain an E-class (ordinary) Student Visa, often referred to as ES.

facts.c: A student visa application needs photos, a letter of acceptance from the institution and proof of money for living and tuition.
facts.q: Letter of acceptance from CamTech or equivalent institution. Proof of financial capability to support living and tuition.

facts.c: A 6-month extension costs around USD 160-170 through an agent or around USD 180 direct, varying by nationality.
facts.q: A 6-month visa extension fee in Cambodia generally costs around $160 to $170 USD when obtained through an agent

facts.note: Conflicts with evisa-kh-type-e-all-countries (E e-visa for all countries).

facts.c: A tourist visa can be extended only once, for one month, at about USD 45.
facts.q: tourist visas allow just one extra month for US$45.

facts.c: Overstaying a visa costs USD 10 a day.
facts.q: Overstaying a visa currently costs US$10 a day.

facts.c: A tourist visa does not allow re-entry; people seeking work are told to take a business visa.
facts.q: Those seeking work in Cambodia should opt for a business visa

facts.c: A child born in Cambodia to foreign parents gets Khmer nationality only if both parents were themselves born and living legally in Cambodia.
facts.q: any child who is born from a foreign mother and father (parents) who were born and living legally in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

facts.c: A child with one Khmer parent is Khmer regardless of place of birth.
facts.q: any legitimate child who is born from a parent ( a mother or father) who has Khmer nationality/ citizenship

facts.c: A foreigner married to a Khmer may apply for nationality only after living together three years from registration of the marriage.
facts.q: may demand for Khmer nationality/citizenship only if upon such man or women have been living together for a period of three (3) years, after registration of a marriage certificate.

facts.c: Naturalisation needs seven years' continuous residence from receipt of a residence card under the Immigration Law, and is a discretionary favour.
facts.q: has been living continuously for seven (7) years from the date of reception of a residence card

facts.c: Naturalisation is not a right and may be refused at discretion.
facts.q: Naturalization is not a right of the applicant, but only a favour of the Kingdom of Cambodia.

facts.c: A foreigner who holds or uses a Khmer identity card or Cambodian passport faces 5 to 10 years' imprisonment.
facts.q: Any foreigner who holds or uses identity card of Khmer nationality or passports of the Kingdom of Cambodia, shall be punished to imprisonment from 5 (five) years to 10 (ten) years.

facts.c: Children born to parents who were born abroad, or who are living in Cambodia illegally, cannot gain Cambodian citizenship.
facts.q: Children born to parents who themselves were born outside of the country or who were born within the country but are considered to be illegally residing in the country will not be able to gain citizenship.

facts.c: Cambodia has ratified the 1951 Refugee Convention but not the two statelessness conventions.

facts.c: Every live birth must be registered at the commune/sangkat office within 30 days (Law on Civil Registration, Vital Statistics and Identification 2023, Arts 17-19).

facts.c: Two foreigners living legally in Cambodia may marry under Cambodian law (Art. 77).

facts.c: A marriage is legal only if registered before the civil registrar at the commune/sangkat (Art. 70).
